safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 days to 1.72 days — current ERP value is overstated by 74% relative to empirical lead time data.

narrative: Material PL1__M84A42A1 exhibits lumpy/erratic demand with a CV of 0.636 and 9.1% zero-demand days, indicating irregular but mostly active consumption. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.939, mean=0.89 days), which inflates the demand-during-lead-time uncertainty and necessitates a meaningful safety stock buffer of 3,062 units to achieve the 95% service level. An EOQ-based (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: order 11,340 units whenever stock falls to the reorder point of 6,428 units, reducing annual total costs by 53% versus the current SAP policy of ordering at MOQ with zero safety stock.
warnings: High demand variability (CV=0.64): robust MAD-based safety stock recommended as cross-check.
High lead time variability (CV=0.94): supplier delivery performance requires active monitoring.
SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days is over-specified; recommend reducing to 1.72 days based on empirical data.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has predominantly non-zero demand (90.9%) and moderate-to-high CV (0.64), making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. It provides a fixed order quantity (EOQ-calibrated) triggered at a stochastic reorder point, balancing ordering and holding costs while maintaining the 95% service level under demand and lead time uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (24,563 units) is not binding: safety stock (3,062) + order quantity (11,340) = 14,402 units, leaving 10,161 units of headroom. No capacity-driven cost penalty applies.
research_insights.escalation_flag: High combined variability (demand CV=0.64, lead time CV=0.94) warrants quarterly review of supplier SLAs and safety stock parameters. If lead time variance increases further, safety stock may need upward revision.
